subject: Mathematics
source: Original supplementary learning draft aligned to Class 6 Ganita Prakash Chapter 4 (fegp104.pdf), Reprint 2026–27. Verify any school-specific edition before publication.
goals: Explain what data are and why they are collected.
Organise counts using tally marks and frequency tables.
Read and create pictographs and bar graphs with clear labels.
Choose a sensible scale and draw conclusions supported by data.
summary: Data are facts or measurements collected to answer a question. Organising data in tables, tally marks, pictographs and bar graphs helps reveal patterns that are difficult to notice in an unorganised list.

concepts.title: Data and frequency
concepts.explanation: Data are collected observations or values. Frequency tells how many times a category or value occurs. A frequency table makes a long list easier to compare.
concepts.example: If 6 students choose cricket, the frequency for cricket is 6.

concepts.title: Tally marks
concepts.explanation: Tally marks are grouped in fives to make counting easier. The fifth mark crosses the first four, so totals can be checked quickly.
concepts.example: A tally group of five plus two extra marks represents 7.

concepts.title: Pictographs
concepts.explanation: A pictograph uses symbols to represent quantities. Its key must say what each symbol stands for; a half symbol can represent half the key value if the scale allows it.
concepts.example: If one book symbol represents 4 books, three symbols represent 12 books.

concepts.title: Bar graphs and scale
concepts.explanation: A bar graph compares categories using bars of equal width. Categories are placed on one axis and frequency on the other. Labels, a title and a consistent scale are essential.
concepts.example: If one grid interval represents 2 students, a bar reaching 5 intervals represents 10 students.

workedExamples.question: Favourite fruit counts are mango 8, banana 5 and apple 7. Which is most popular and how many students were counted?
steps: The largest frequency is 8 for mango.
workedExamples.answer: Mango is most popular; 20 students were counted.

workedExamples.question: A pictograph key says one symbol represents 3 books. How many books do 4 symbols represent?
steps: Multiply the number of symbols by the key value: 4 × 3.

practice.question: What does frequency mean in a data table?
practice.answer: The number of times a value or category occurs.

practice.question: Why must a pictograph include a key?
practice.answer: The key tells the reader how much quantity each symbol represents.
practice.why: Without a key, the symbol count cannot be converted reliably.

practice.question: A bar graph scale is 1 division = 5 children. A bar is 4 divisions high. What is its value?
Why should a graph have a title and labels?
practice.answer: They tell the reader what is being compared and what the axes represent.
practice.why: A graph needs context to be interpreted correctly.

mcqs.why: Frequency is the count for a category or value.

mcqs.q: A pictograph key is used to…
mcqs.why: The key connects symbols with quantities.

mcqs.q: Which is essential in a bar graph?
mcqs.why: Labels and scale make comparisons meaningful.

mcqs.q: Counts are 3, 8, 6 and 4. The greatest count is…
mcqs.why: Eight is the largest of the four values.

mcqs.q: If 1 symbol represents 2 objects, 5 symbols represent…

revision: Data are collected facts; frequency is a count.
Tally marks group counts to make them easier to check.
A bar graph needs a title, labelled axes, categories and a consistent scale.
Describe only patterns that the data actually support.

chapterTest.instructions: Answer independently before opening the answer guide. Show steps for calculations.

questions.q: Explain why data are organised before drawing a graph.
questions.answer: Organisation makes counts clear and helps prevent errors when representing or comparing categories.

questions.q: A key says one symbol equals 5 votes. What do 6 symbols represent?
Name three features of a clear bar graph.
questions.answer: Any three: title, labelled axes, categories, consistent scale, equal-width bars and readable values.
